title: Why God comes as a person
hookLine: why would God come as a person, and wait at a shore?
carry: avatar: god comes down to show us how
tomorrow: the throne of Ayodhya has no king on it. so what's sitting there?

lines: RAMA ASKS THE SEA, AND WAITS.
cards: Anyone can post advice. It lands differently when you watch someone live it. Rama stands at the edge of the sea.
Sita is on the far side, in Lanka, and between them there's only water. So he asks the ocean to make a way, and waits. Nothing.
He waits longer. At last he raises his bow, and the ocean itself rises out of the waves and offers a way across. The question under the scene: why would God come as a person at all?

teach.b: The Bhagavata Purana gives an answer in Hanuman's words.
The Lord came as a human being, he says, to teach human beings. That's the key to avatar, the word for Vishnu's comings: it means descent. Vishnu as the boar lifts the earth from the waters.
Vishnu as Rama waits at a shore, asks first, loses his patience, keeps his promises, grieves, misses his wife. He does what a person does, so people can watch how it's done.
Here's one place a neighbor says something close.
Christians read in the Gospel of John: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.”
Later in the same Gospel, after Jesus washes his friends' feet, he says: “For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.”

Two traditions, each saying God came close enough to be watched, and copied. And an honest difference. Christians hold that God became human once, in Jesus, and that his life, death and rising save the world.
The Puranas tell of Vishnu coming down again and again, in many forms, age after age, Rama among them. Neither account needs the other's to mean what it means.
So when the ocean finally rises for Rama, it isn't only a god's power on show.
It's a man who asked first.

how: Rama's name is sung in homes and temples, and his birth is celebrated at Rama Navami; the Bhagavata's short telling of his life is read alongside the longer Ramayanas.

o: the prince of Ayodhya: Vishnu come as a human
the god of the ocean who rises from the waves
a monkey hero who leaps across the sea

games.q: who said it — tap the pairs.
p: I have given you an example

s: Rama raises his bow before he ever asks the ocean
he asks first and waits; the bow comes last.
Hindus and Christians believe the same thing about God becoming human
both say God came close enough to be watched; Christians hold it happened once, in Jesus, and the Puranas tell of many descents.
in the Bhagavata, Hanuman says the Lord came as a human to teach humans
that's the Purana's reason for this form.

games.q: your little sister ignores everything you tell her about homework, but copies whatever you actually do. what does today's lesson suggest?
o: do it where she can see; people learn from a life they can watch.
tell her again, more firmly; she'll get it eventually.
leave it to your parents; it isn't really your job.
games.why: the Puranas' Rama comes as a human to teach humans, and in John, Jesus says: I have given you an example.

practice: Listen to your own breath coming in and going out, like small waves at a shore. Let each wave arrive in its own time, without pulling it in or pushing it out. If you pray, you can wait there, the way Rama waited at the water.

wordCard.voice: Rama: in the Puranas, Vishnu come as a human being, to teach human beings how a life is lived.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Rama, the prince of Ayodhya; in the Puranas, Vishnu come as a human.

carryVoice: Keep this one: avatar, God comes down to show us how. Rama asked the ocean first, and then waited. Back tomorrow.
